notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, site and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 3 simply supported 35-ft bays, W33X387 girders, one 30-ton cab crane, on new freestanding W14X730 columns with welded twin-rib bracket seats, base plates, anchor rods and spread footings, and crane-level rod X-bracing; the existing building carries no crane load. Seismic: ordinary steel cantilever column system across the runway and rod bracing not specifically detailed for seismic resistance along it, Seismic Design Category B. Fixed at both ends at this reach, the paired bars cannot follow the girder end rotation and thermal travel along the runway (the tie movement checks over their limits): the column gusset slides 14 mm each way along the runway on longer sleeves (column-end slide, fillers at the girder gusset; checks tie-slide-*). Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier. The bracket stays: the W10X112 crane-level strut is moment-connected in plan at every column by 13 mm plates on its flanges (torsion brace, 3 rows of bolt pairs) and holds the new W14X730 columns against the twist: 0.0073 rad factored (limit 0.02) and 2 mm of bearing movement at every crane start and stop (limit 24 mm). The girder's twist movement under the factored traction is 3 mm, above the 2 mm (a configurator target, tightened from 1/8 in where the tie could not take the movement, not a code limit): the W10X112 is the stiffest strut that fits the torsion plates, and the tie, slots and gaps take this movement in their checks. With the strut on the column centerline alone, the girder seated 792 mm off the column axis, the traction twists the column 0.0162 rad factored (limit 0.02) and 5 mm of bearing movement at every crane start and stop (limit 24 mm).

selections.reason: The support reaction, about 505 kN (115 kip), is above the AIST TR-13 §5.9.2 guideline of 222 kN (50 kip) for column brackets, a clause to be verified: consider column caps over the new columns; an advisory, not a code limit, so the support entered (Welded twin-rib seat) is kept and checked here.

Fixed at both ends at this reach, the paired bars cannot follow the girder end rotation and thermal travel along the runway (the tie movement checks over their limits): the column gusset slides 14 mm each way along the runway on longer sleeves (column-end slide, fillers at the girder gusset; checks tie-slide-*). With the column face left free to its 762 mm limit (the tie sizing took it to 762 mm), the runway built and calculated with the column, base and tie sized for it does not pass either (base-drift 1.83, column-drift 1.10): the face stays at 508 mm.

Lightest compact W within the sizing targets (ratio ≤ 0.85, deflections ≤ 0.9 of the limits): screening estimates, top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 0.61, vertical deflection 0.25, lateral 0.65 and rail-head movement with twist 0.83 of their limits; flanges at least 267 mm wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 9 by deflection, 98 by sizing ratio, 63 by flange width; the next lighter, W24X370: lateral deflection 0.91 of the limit > 0.9; rail-head movement with twist 0.99 of the limit > 0.9. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios.

New cantilever column for a 30-ton crane (W14X120 to 5 t, W14X159 to 12.5 t, W14X211 to 25 t, else W14X257). The W14X257 chosen for the crane gives base drift ratio 4.74 > 0.9: no W14 to the W14X730 meets the new column's drift, torsion and twist ratios for this crane; the heaviest searched, W14X730, lowers the governing ratio and is built, giving base drift ratio 0.99 > 0.9 (configurator estimate, within the calculation's limits).

selections.designed: paired-bars, closest; tie to be designed by hand
selections.reason: Top-flange tie not resolved: the Paired flat bars on a flange saddle, as sized for the estimated tie demands, still exceeds tie-move-strength 2.09 (configurator estimates), and no other tie arrangement the configurator tries fits and passes here. Recommended: column caps over the new columns (support column-cap): the girder bears on the column axis, so the traction no longer twists the column at a bracket seat, and the end fork on the cap (the girder's bearing stiffeners with the couple of its bearing bolts) replaces the top-flange tie; the configurator does not build that alternative here. Otherwise design the tie connection by hand.

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints tight (gap 1/16 in max.), supplier's joint bars (deferred submittal) installed slip-critical: Class A surfaces, bolts pretensioned, re-tightened at 30 and 90 days.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
